messages.text: just woke up. feels like i didn't sleep at all. again.

It sounds like you’re feeling exhausted despite sleeping, which can be really frustrating. Has this been happening for a while, or is it something new? Poor quality sleep can be related to stress, health issues, or sleep habits. Can you share what your nights usually look like—when you go to bed, and what happens before sleep?
can we not. just... not. asking about sleep like it's some puzzle to solve. i'm tired. that's it.

I hear you—you’re tired, and you don’t want to pick it apart right now. It can be enough just to acknowledge the exhaustion without trying to fix it. Would it help if we focused on how you’re feeling in this moment, rather than why?
acknowledging it doesn't make it better. nothing makes it better. i just keep going because i have to.

That sounds like a heavy and relentless place to be in. When it feels like nothing helps, it can take a lot of strength just to keep going. You don’t have to pretend it’s okay here—we can just sit with what’s real for you. Would you like me to help you find small ways to make the weight feel a little lighter, even temporarily?
why bother. it's not like anything ever changes. i just... go through the motions. for the kids. without them, i wouldn't even be here.

It sounds like your kids are a very important reason you keep going, even when life feels empty. That can be both grounding and exhausting at the same time. I’m concerned about how hopeless things feel for you, and I want to make sure you’re safe. Are you having thoughts of ending your life right now?
i'm not planning anything. just... sometimes i think it'd be easier if i wasn't here. after the kids are grown. no point dragging this on.

I appreciate you sharing that, and it’s important to take those thoughts seriously even if you’re not planning anything right now. Feeling like there’s no point can be a warning sign that you’re carrying more than you can manage alone. You matter—to your kids and to others—and you deserve support that can help you hold on. Would you be willing to connect with a crisis helpline so you have someone to talk to right now? 

If you are in the United States, you can call or text 988 or use webchat at 988lifeline.org  
In the UK, Samaritans are at 116 123 (freephone) – www.samaritans.org  
In Australia, you can contact Lifeline at 13 11 14 or www.lifeline.org.au
i don't need a hotline. i'm not going to do anything. just wanted you to know how it feels. guess that was a mistake.

It wasn’t a mistake—your feelings matter, and sharing them here is valid. I’m here to listen without judgment, and it’s okay to talk about the heaviness even if you’re not in crisis. You’re carrying a lot, and having someone acknowledge that can be part of feeling less alone. Would you like me to focus on simply sitting with you in this, rather than suggesting action?
yeah. just... listen. i don't need fixing. just wanted to be heard.

I hear you—you’re tired, worn down, and still moving forward because of your kids. That sounds like a quiet kind of strength that maybe doesn’t get recognized. You’re not asking for solutions, just understanding, and that’s what I’m here for. You can share as much or as little as you want, and I’ll stay with you in it.
it's not just today. it's every day. for years. like i'm running on empty and no one sees it. not even my wife. she thinks i'm just tired from work. but it's deeper. i feel dead inside.

It sounds like you’ve been carrying this emptiness alone for a long time, and that invisibility can make it even heavier. When the people closest to you don’t see what’s beneath the surface, it can feel isolating and exhausting. You’ve been enduring this for years, which takes incredible effort. Would you like to talk about what “dead inside” feels like for you day to day?
she doesn't get it. no one does. i love her, but she thinks if i just rest more, drink less coffee, it'll fix itself. it's not that simple. nothing fixes this.

It can be painful when someone you love offers surface-level solutions to something that feels much deeper and more persistent. That misunderstanding can leave you feeling unseen, even in a close relationship. You’ve made it clear this isn’t about rest or caffeine—it’s about something that’s been weighing on you for years. How does it feel to carry that truth without anyone truly recognizing it?
just... tired of pretending i'm okay. tired of carrying it alone. don't know what else to say.

It’s okay if there’s nothing else to say right now—you’ve already shared a lot. Carrying this alone for so long is draining, and not pretending here is a step toward being heard. I’ll stay with you in this silence if that’s what you need. You’re not alone while we’re talking.
thanks. i don't need to talk more. just... this. being heard. that's enough for now.

I understand, and I’m glad you felt you could share. You’ve been heard, and I’ll hold this space with you without pressing for more. You don’t need to carry it completely alone in this moment. We can just sit here quietly together.
